page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance powered by the ARM-based AWS Graviton4 processor, built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. Managed by the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation is set at 8.0 GB, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio typical of memory-intensive footprints. It includes 59 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are present on this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate single-threaded efficiency alongside strict single-core throughput boundaries. Single-core execution reflects solid IPC, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1741.0 and a stress-ng single-core metric of 1694.58, both ranking in the middle tier. In single-threaded compression benchmarks, the core achieves 30.04 GB/sec in gzip and a top-quartile 14.0 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate multi-core metrics naturally reflect the single-core hardware ceiling, with total PassMark CPU scoring at 986.83 and Redis operations reaching 2.45 million SET operations per second.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, r8gd.medium provides a cost-effective point of entry into the Graviton4 memory-optimized family with integrated high-speed local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff centers on core parallelism; with only 1 vCPU, CPU-bound concurrent workloads will quickly face bottlenecks. The instance is suited for lightweight caching layers, small in-memory databases, development environments, Redis or KeyDB testing, and low-concurrency data transformation tasks requiring rapid scratch-disk access and high memory per core.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.medium is a memory-optimized instance featuring 1 dedicated ARM64 vCPU powered by an AWS Graviton4 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The server includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a substantial 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, paired with 59 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network link. With no dedicated GPU hardware, its processing capabilities focus strictly on energy-efficient CPU compute. Benchmark performance displays competent single-threaded results, evidenced by average Geekbench single-core scores and high bzip3 decompression rates, while aggregate multi-core throughput remains constrained by the single-thread execution limit. This instance is best suited for small-scale memory-intensive workloads, localized caching tiers, development setups, and single-threaded batch tasks requiring local NVMe storage.
